answer: The tundra drift fence proves one person: a fence a flock can test. The claimant raises a drift fence across a pass below the summit, then wharf shepherds drive a flock through the gap at dawn as the claimant counts the animals past the gate. Two wardens recount the flock and check the stakes within four days. A gap in the fence, a count that disagrees, or a flock driven twice voids the season, burns a 180-credit stake and bars the workshop two seasons. Fencing 1,000 fake passes means 1,000 fences and 1,000 flocks counted by hand, while one honest claimant fences a pass before dusk.
